pl-l1d23c6-d1e105.summary: States that as there is no diversity in the Trinity, neither is there multiplicity, so God should be called not multiple but triune and simple.
claims: God is not multiple but triune and simple.

pl-l1d23c6-d1e107.summary: Cites Ambrose, De Trinitate I: in Father and Son there is one divinity, not discordant, neither confused (being one) nor multiple (being undifferentiated). So God is not multiple.
claims: The divinity of Father and Son is one, unconfused, and not multiple.

pl-l1d23c6.summary: Adds that, as there is no diversity in the Trinity, so there is no multiplicity; God is to be called not multiple but triune and simple. Ambrose: in Father and Son there is one undivided divinity, neither confused nor multiple, so God is not multiple.
claims: There is no multiplicity in the Trinity.
God is triune and simple, not multiple.
The one divinity of Father and Son is neither confused nor multiple.
